MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. 50 eggs are packed in trays that each hold 8 eggs. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 6
   C. 7
   D. 8

2. Ali writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 7/4
   B. 5/12
   C. 3/8
   D. 1 3/4

3. Work out 12 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 262
   B. 36
   C. 252
   D. 242

4. What is the 5th multiple of 6? (1 mark)
   A. 30
   B. 11
   C. 24
   D. 36

5. Round 765 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 700
   B. 780
   C. 770
   D. 760

6. Change 210 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 3 h
   B. 4 h
   C. 4 h 30 min
   D. 3 h 30 min

7. A 50 kg sack of rice is packed into bags of 5 kg. How many bags are filled? (1 mark)
   A. 250
   B. 5
   C. 45
   D. 10

8. A pencil starts at the 0 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 7 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 9 cm
   B. 7 cm
   C. 6 cm
   D. 8 cm

9. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many are NOT lorry? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 11
   C. 1
   D. 10

10. Why can 2a + 3b not be written as 5ab? (1 mark)
   A. Because 2 + 3 is not 5
   B. Because letters can only be added to numbers
   C. Because ab is not a letter
   D. a and b are different things, so the terms cannot be joined

11. Beth writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/2
   B. 11/5
   C. 2/9
   D. 9/9

12. Cuboid A is 10 by 2 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 5 by 4 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. Cuboid A
   B. It cannot be told
   C. Cuboid B
   D. They are equal

13. A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875 of them. How many seedlings are left? (1 mark)
   A. 4,375 seedlings
   B. 3,625 seedlings
   C. 3,725 seedlings
   D. 3,615 seedlings

14. One county has 7,300 pupils and a smaller county has 4,562 pupils. How many more pupils does the bigger county have? (1 mark)
   A. 2,838 pupils
   B. 3,262 pupils
   C. 2,738 pupils
   D. 2,728 pupils

15. Which object does NOT have a right angle at its corners? (1 mark)
   A. A book
   B. A door
   C. A round plate
   D. A window

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 5, 9, 13, 17, ... and state the rule. (3 marks)

17. Wanjiru saves Ksh 250 every week. Write how much she has saved after 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 weeks. State the rule. (3 marks)

18. A farmer joins 4 pieces of wire, each measuring 2 m 30 cm, to make one long wire. Find the length of the long wire. (3 marks)

19. Start at 10,000 and subtract 1,500 each time. Write the first five numbers of the pattern. (3 marks)

20. A trip costs Ksh t for each pupil. Write an expression for the cost for 20 pupils and find the cost if t = 150. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 7
   50 ÷ 8 = 6 remainder 2. The 2 left-over eggs need one more tray, so 7 trays are needed.

2. A — 7/4
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 7/4 is one whole or more.

3. C — 252
   12 × 1 = 12 and 12 × 20 = 240. 12 + 240 = 252.

4. A — 30
   Multiply 6 × 5 = 30. It is the 5th multiple of 6.

5. C — 770
   Look at the ones digit 5. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 765 rounds to 770.

6. D — 3 h 30 min
   210 ÷ 60 = 3 remainder 30, so 210 minutes = 3 h 30 min.

7. D — 10
   50 ÷ 5 = 10 bags.

8. B — 7 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 7 − 0 = 7 cm.

9. A — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

10. D — a and b are different things, so the terms cannot be joined
   a and b stand for different kinds of things, so 2a and 3b are not like terms. The expression stays as 2a + 3b.

11. C — 2/9
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 2/9 is less than one whole.

12. C — Cuboid B
   A = 10 × 2 × 2 = 40 blocks. B = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

13. B — 3,625 seedlings
   Subtract 6,500 − 2,875 = 3,625. Check by adding: 3,625 + 2,875 = 6,500.

14. C — 2,738 pupils
   Subtract 7,300 − 4,562 = 2,738. Check by adding: 2,738 + 4,562 = 7,300.

15. C — A round plate
   A round plate has a curved edge and no corners, so no right angles.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rule: add 4. Next numbers: 21, 25, 29.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers (1 mark if only two are correct).

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: 250, 500, 750, 1,000, 1,250. Rule: add 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for correct numbers.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 230 × 4 = 920 cm (2 marks); 920 cm = 9 m 20 cm (1 mark).

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000, 8,500, 7,000, 5,500, 4,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct rule and 2 marks for the numbers.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20t. When t = 150, cost = 20 × 150 = Ksh 3,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 20t, 1 mark for replacing t by 150, 1 mark for Ksh 3,000.
